references.text: The context verse explaining who Eldad and Medad were, and that they prophesied in the camp after the Spirit rested on them.
Joshua's reaction to the news that Eldad and Medad were prophesying, and Moses' response expressing his wish that all of the Lord's people were prophets.
A young man runs to bring news, a similar pattern where a young messenger reports important events.
A young man runs to bring news to a leader, the same narrative pattern with a young messenger.
Saul prophesies unexpectedly among the prophets, a similar situation where someone prophesies outside the expected group.
The Spirit of God comes upon people who begin to prophesy unexpectedly, parallel to Eldad and Medad prophesying in the camp.
Joel's prophecy that God will pour out His Spirit on all flesh and that everyone will prophesy, as Moses wished in verse 29.
The disciples report about someone casting out demons in Jesus' name who does not belong to their group, a similar situation where someone exercises spiritual ministry outside the established group.
John reports about one who casts out demons in Jesus' name without following them, parallel to the reporting about Eldad and Medad prophesying outside the tent.
